sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have both spoken of their desire for the benefits bill to come down, but the government has not yet laid out a timetable for any reductions.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Their political opponents have criticised them for a lack of detail on welfare reform in Wednesday's Budget, accusing the government of delaying difficult decisions over cuts.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Official forecasts released alongside the Budget indicate welfare spending is going to increase by £79bn in cash terms over the next few years.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has taken a look at the numbers behind this thorny political issue and some of the difficult options the government have to bring down welfare costs.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The official forecaster, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), estimates in its latest forecasts that the cost of the welfare system will rise , external from £353bn this year to £431bn in 2032.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The OBR's figures include spending on pensioners, which accounts for just under half of the total.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The majority of this cost is on the state pension.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: However, if we look at the size of welfare spending relative to the size of the overall economy the OBR's projections are less dramatic, increasing from 11.1% today to 11.3% of GDP in 2032.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Total welfare spending would also remain below the peak of around 12% of GDP in 2013 following the global financial crisis, leading some economists and researchers to question the idea that welfare spending is out of control. , external But there are some welfare costs that are rising rapidly.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Spending on health and disability related benefits, in particular Personal Independence Payments (PIP), is up sharply since the Covid-19 pandemic.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Accounting for inflation, spending on working-age disability benefits increased from £14bn in 2020 to £25bn in 2026 , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Inflation-adjusted welfare spending remains lower than 2013 because several other working-age benefits, such as Universal Credit and housing benefit, were cut by Conservative-led governments as part of their austerity programme from 2010 onwards , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: So spending in some parts of the system has come down while it has risen in others - and there could be a connection.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Some researchers think the post-2010 welfare cuts to benefits might have created an incentive for people to claim sickness and disability benefits instead to protect their living standards , external , therefore shifting costs around the system rather than generating lasting savings.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Many also see a specific problem regarding the growing number of young people in the welfare system claiming benefits, including PIP.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Official figures show the number of 16 to 24-year-olds who are not in employment, education or training (Neets) has risen , external by around 230,000 since 2019 to just under one million.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn is leading an official review into Neets and is expected to recommend major reforms designed to get many off benefits and into work.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: His interim report in May estimated that annual PIP expenditure on 16 to 24-year-olds rose from £1.3bn in 2020 to around £3.2bn in 2025 , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: It also projected this cost would reach £6.5bn and cover 700,000 young people in five years' time.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: PIP claimants can be in work, but official statistics show that only around one in five are , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Politicians are often unclear about what they mean by reducing spending on welfare.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: In March 2025, former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer's government presented a plan which it said would save £5bn a year from health-related welfare spending by 2030 by tightening PIP access and reducing the value of health-related Universal Credit payments.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: But official forecasts made it clear that annual spending on health-related welfare in cash terms was still set to rise after the reform , external , just not as rapidly as the path it had previously been on.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: However, at the time the OBR did forecast the plans would help put overall UK welfare spending on a "slightly downward trajectory" as a share of the economy , external over the medium term, rather than remaining flat as had been previously projected.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: So this type of relative reduction in anticipated welfare spending, rather than a cut in absolute cash terms, could be what the government seeks to deliver.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The final Milburn report is expected in the coming weeks, as well as a separate final report from disability minister Stephen Timms into the options for PIP reform.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: There has been speculation that these could recommend creating a new welfare system for people under the age of 25 , external , so they are not eligible for PIP and receive lower payments than older people.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: There are also suggestions Timms could propose a new PIP eligibility test to reduce access , external , although he was not specifically instructed to find savings.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Reforms along these lines could potentially make some savings to the welfare bill relative to the existing trajectory of rising spending, as well as reducing forecast welfare spending as share of GDP.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: But some analysts argue that to be effective in delivering sustainable savings, such reforms are likely also to require the government to spend a lot more , external to enable young people in particular to get into and remain in work.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: This was signalled by the interim Milburn report which noted that for every £1 the government spends on employment support for young people around £25 is spent on benefits , suggesting he could propose a significant increase in government spending on welfare-to-work schemes.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: This means that any welfare savings could, in the near term at least, be offset by additional spending in other departments.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: However, in the long term this approach could still deliver welfare savings if the employment support was effective.

sentences.text: The guitar George Michael performed with in his 1987 Faith music video has sold for £180,000 at auction, after a row over the sale of memorabilia related to the singer.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: The guitar was one of more than 30 items auctioned by Sworders from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, Michael's long-time personal assistant.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: The sale fetched a total of £238,000 excluding buyers' premium.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: Bailey died in 2014 and the items were sold by her estranged husband Ian Belcher, who inherited them after her death.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: Gerard Bailey, Siobhan's brother, told the BBC she "would be horrified at the prospect of the auction being held in her name and that her personal, cherished possessions are being sold off to the highest bidder".
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: Belcher declined to comment.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: Sworders chairman Guy Schooling said Belcher had been "nothing but delightful" during their interactions over the past two-and-a-half years.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: "There are two ways of looking at this - it can be cashing in, or it can be a bit of a memorial and a tribute to Siobhan, and that's the way we've looked at it," he told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: The auction house billed the 32 lots, including signed photographs, invitations to events and presentation CDs and discs, as a "remarkable group of memorabilia from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, George Michael's long-time personal assistant and trusted confidante".
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: Siobhan was in the process of divorcing Belcher when she died, but was legally still married to him.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: She did not leave a will.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: Her brother claimed she had started to draw up a will shortly before she died, which would have left the items to her nieces and nephews, but it was not registered.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: There is no suggestion that Belcher did not have the right to sell the items, because her estate legally passed to him when she died.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: Bailey said if his sister had lived a few weeks longer, the items would not have passed to Belcher because he would not have been considered her next of kin.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: In a letter to the auction house seen by the BBC, Bailey said the rest of the family considered the auction a "breach of [Siobhan's] privacy", adding that the use of her name was "disingenuous" and "wholly unethical".

sentences.text: He told the auction house that Belcher's "misuse of my sister's name" was "frankly dishonourable", and profiteering from the items was "egregiously shameful".
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: Bailey asked that the auction should not go ahead, or be in Belcher's name rather than Siobhan's.
sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.article_title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row

sentences.text: At a recycling plant in Coventry, I watched staff sorting rubbish on a fast-moving conveyor belt when a crushed yellow sharps container suddenly appeared among the waste.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: "A resident has put this in a wheelie bin," explained supervisor Paul Pagett.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: "It then gets crushed by the recycling vehicle and then it comes to us open and obviously we've got needles then falling out on to the line putting my guys at risk." The sharps box should never have been there.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: Used needles should be disposed of separately through dedicated clinical waste services.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: Instead, recycling bosses say they are increasingly finding them mixed in with household waste.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: "There are safe disposal routes for needles but the worst place to put them is in your recycling," said Richard Dobbs, managing director of Sherborne Recycling.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: "It ends up in facilities like ours where it will be touched by people and that's inherently unsafe." Paul Pagett said discarded needles were putting workers at risk Sherborne Recycling handles waste from several local authorities and serves about 1.5 million residents.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: The plant is highly automated, but workers still have to remove items that cannot be processed and regularly inspect waste to check what is being sent for recycling.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: That means employees can potentially come into direct contact with discarded needles.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: Paul Pagett showed me a cupboard stacked with yellow sharps containers that have all been recovered from the recycling stream since the start of the year.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: Some are likely to have come from people using medicines such as insulin, where patients are often given sharps bins and advice on disposal.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: But recycling bosses say the growing popularity of privately prescribed weight-loss injections has created a new challenge.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: Workers must sift through waste by hand to remove items that cannot be processed Many people buy the drugs privately and may not automatically receive a sharps box or guidance on how to dispose of used needles safely.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: The result is that large numbers are ending up in household bins and, in some cases, recycling collections.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: For workers, the consequences can be serious.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: Dobbs described what happens when someone accidentally sticks themselves with a used needle.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: You have to be tested and wait for results.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: It can take months," he said.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: In other recycling plants, dozens of workers might be exposed.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: The advice is simple: Speak to your GP or pharmacy about obtaining a sharps bin and how to dispose of it safely.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: Whatever you do, never put a sharps container or loose needles in your recycling bin.
sentences.article_title: Weight-loss jabs boom putting recycling centre workers at risk

sentences.text: "I just needed a hot meal to keep going for my daughter," Sophie said A first-time mum was denied hospital meals while her baby was "fighting for her life" because she was not breastfeeding.

sentences.text: Sophie Price, 22, was "shocked" when staff refused to give her a meal while her daughter Florence was being treated on a paediatric ward at Grange University Hospital in Cwmbran, Torfaen.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Despite giving birth in the hospital five days earlier, she was told she was no longer classed as a patient as she was not breastfeeding, so she would not be provided with meals.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Aneurin Bevan University Health Board said it was "sorry to hear about Sophie's experience" and was "committed to supporting families throughout their child's stay".
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: "It was just an awful experience.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: I just needed a hot meal to keep going for my daughter," said Sophie, from Newport.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Her family said they spent more than £1,000 on food from the canteen and takeaway meals during their three-week stay at the hospital while Florence was treated.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Sophie said she and her husband were told Florence may "need to be induced into a coma at any point" during her treatment The health board said mothers are provided with meals while under the care of hospital maternity services as both them and their baby are classed as patients, whether they are breastfeeding or not.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: But on paediatric wards, only the child is classed as the patient, however the hospital's policy is to provide breastfeeding mums with meals as this directly supports the baby's feeding and nutrition.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: For babies who are formula-fed, the health board said formula was "provided as needed" by the hospital, but Sophie said she was told she would need to bring it in herself.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Sophie had only left the hospital - which earlier this week denied online claims it was "dangerous" and "dreadful" - for 24 hours before she and her husband Ryli Price had to return when they realised Florence was not able to breathe and the "colour started to drain from her".
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: "Florence started to make some really harsh grunting sounds, it sounded like a death rattle coming from her chest up into her mouth," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Sophie ran into the A&E department screaming "she's not breathing" and credited the quick response of medical staff who helped save her daughter's life.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Florence was diagnosed with bronchiolitis , external , rhinoviruses - which causes the common cold , external - and a blood infection, which meant her lungs could not operate on their own.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: She was placed on a machine that pumped air into her lungs via a mask.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: The first-time parents spent three weeks in hospital with their daughter Florence Sophie said despite being "hungry and exhausted" she was denied a meal while her daughter was "in intensive care fighting for her life".
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: "Imagine being in a hospital with your seriously ill baby on breathing support monitors, overwhelmed with worry, anxiety and stress, only to be told you aren't entitled to a meal because you're formula feeding instead of breastfeeding," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Sophie said she was bleeding through her clothes and "in a lot of pain" as her hips had to be put back in place after being dislocated during childbirth.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: At one point, Sophie said she realised she had not eaten for about 28 hours and remembered seeing a food trolley being brought round to mums on the ward.
sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: She said: "I remember them saying to me 'oh hi mum, hope you're OK, are you hungry?' And me saying 'oh yeah, I'm absolutely starving, I haven't eaten in ages.

sentences.text: What have you got?'" Sophie was asked if she was breastfeeding, which she had not been able to do after the first 24 hours of Florence's life as she was no longer taking to her breast milk.

sentences.article_title: Mum of critically ill baby denied hospital food as she wasn't breastfeeding

sentences.text: Ofcom has set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Under the UK's social media ban - which is due to come into force in March next year - those under that age will be prevented from accessing ten of the biggest platforms, including Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Many UK adults are also likely to have to confirm that they are not under-age by using one of the proposed measures, which are subject to government approval.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: A similar ban was introduced in Australia last year but many children there have found ways to get round it .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: The UK says it intends to take a tougher approach.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Age verification below 18 is challenging because 16 and 17 year olds don't have credit cards or full driving licences, and may not have passports either.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: They can also look significantly older or younger than they are.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: However, ultimately it will be up to the tech companies to figure out how to implement the checks: the onus is on social network providers to come up with their own solutions and comply.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Meta told the BBC it already applies some methods recommended by Ofcom to enforce its user age requirements or place users in Teen Accounts settings.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But it said applying age checks at device-level, via app stores, could reduce the burden on people to have to repeatedly verify their age across multiple platforms.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: This would place responsibility with Apple and Google, who between them operate most of the world's smartphones.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Apple has already introduced age verification in the UK .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: However Ofcom says that would not absolve the social network providers from doing their own checks as well.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Dawes said making the ban work would be a joint effort.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "At Ofcom, what we will do is make sure that the services that the social media companies put in the checks that they need to," she told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "That's our job, but the wider question about how everybody engages with this, it is for everybody, really.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Child safety campaigners including the Molly Rose Foundation and NSPCC welcomed Ofcom's guidance.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But both said there were lessons to be learned from how Australia's social media ban had been implemented, after it was found many under-16s could still access social platforms .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "That's why, as we prepare to embark on our own social media ban in the UK, we need to make sure we accurately know the age of child users," said Rani Govender, head of child safety online at the NSPCC.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: She said the government and Ofcom must ensure tech firms are held accountable for meeting age check standards "to help keep children safe online and ensure the ban delivers change in practice".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But Andy Burrows, the Molly Rose Foundation's chief executive, said Ofcom had shown a "dire track record" of enforcing the Online Safety Act - raising questions over how effectively it would help deliver a social media ban.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "Andy Burnham must deliver a ban that learns the lessons from Australia and that incentivises safety-by-design as the price of admission to the UK market, with a ban as the starting point in a proper plan to give children a safe and happy online life," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Jonny Blunt, corporate affairs director of BT's consumer division, said families should "prepare children for life online after the ban and highlight the risks of trying to dodge the restrictions".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "Having those conversations now and giving young people time to prepare for the changes in March will be crucial in helping them adapt to a significant change for a whole generation," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: The US Federal Reserve has held interest rates steady at 3.75% - 4%.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The decision comes within a week of the midterm elections and after the central bank raised interest rates for the first time in three years at its September meeting.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: "The overwhelming consensus, the overwhelming judgement, is that what we've done in this monetary medicine is starting to work some," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said, referring to September's interest rate rise.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Figures published after the Fed's announcement showed the US economy growing at a stronger pace than expected, with inflation running above the Fed's target.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: An interest rate tells people and businesses how much it costs to borrow money – such as with credit cards, mortgages, or business loans – but also what return they get for saving cash.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The Fed influences interest rates in the US through its target range for the federal funds rate, which is the interest rate used by commercial banks for overnight borrowing.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: In its decision to hold rates steady this month, the Fed said that while inflation remains high, it wanted to gather more information before making another decision to change rates.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The Fed also noted that while there was uncertainty, the US economy remained resilient.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Warsh acknowledged that inflation remained too high, but noted that there were other signs - such as tightening credit conditions - that the economy was moving in the right direction.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: There is plenty more economic data to come between now and the committee's next meeting, the Fed chair added, which should paint a more detailed picture of the state of the economy.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: At that point, Warsh said, "we'll be, I think, better positioned to determine the right policy decision and the stance of policy." While last month the committee signalled there could be one more rate rise this year, Warsh would not be drawn out on where he thinks they will go in six weeks' time.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: "A lot of things can happen, so I'm not going to be able to share with you my musings." The decision to hold rates steady was not unanimous.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The US economy grew by 3.4% on an annualised basis in the three months to September, stronger than analysts had expected.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: That strong growth was driven by an acceleration in investment, and strong consumer spending.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: While there was an annualised increase in personal spending of 3.8%, the annualised increase in private investment was a huge 19.4% which analysts say was largely due to investment in artificial intelligence.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Inflation is also above the Fed's target range.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Prices increased by 3.7% in the year to September, driven higher by fuel and energy prices which have surged off the back of the war in Iran.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The Fed uses interest rate changes to try to keep inflation – the rate at which prices change – at 2% a year and keep the job market stable.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: When inflation is too high, the Fed tends to raise interest rates.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: This tends to mean higher rates from banks and other lenders, which in turn affects spending and saving decisions.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: For example, someone refinancing their mortgage or buying a property for the first time could face higher mortgage rates.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: It could also mean higher interest rates on credit cards or car loans.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: However, it means higher interest rates on savings as well.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: This encourages people and businesses to save more, spend less money, and make less investments.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: It also encourages companies to hire less people or slow the pace of pay rises.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: All of this tends to reduce demand and slow inflation.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: When inflation is low or if the Fed believes the economy needs a boost, it cut rates.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The idea is that this will have the opposite affect, with banks dropping rates leading to more spending and less saving from people and businesses.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Leaving the rates unchanged means rates on things like new mortgages or business loans are also less likely to change.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: It also means interest rates on cash savings are unlikely to rise.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: US interest rates have historically moved around quite a bit.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The last time Fed rates were as high as they have been recently was in the lead up to and during the start of the 2008 global financial crisis.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The Fed then dropped rates to historic lows to encourage spending and job creation during the economic slump and kept them at those lows for several years.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: They picked up again ahead of the pandemic before dropping to as low as 0%-0.25% during the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: They then rose to highs of 5.25%-5% from the middle of 2023 to August 2024 as inflation jumped.

sentences.text: If you are an 18-to-20 year-old earning the minimum wage, your pay will go up by 3.9% from next April.

sentences.text: Mohammed Ashim is paid to film his hands at work Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working." He wears the camera for five or six hours a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "It's good money, but honestly, the feeling of doing something this futuristic is what keeps me excited.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I never imagined my razor techniques would be useful to a global tech company," says Ashim.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: He is one of hundreds of thousands of workers across the world paid to record their activities.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That video is then sold on to technology companies and research organisations who use it to train artificial intelligence - in particular so-called physical AI, a type of artificial intelligence that can control robots in the real world.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Every robotics company, every frontier AI lab, has a specific kind of data they want: industrial tasks, agriculture, household chores, small business work like pottery, garment-making, embroidery, candle-making.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: His company pays $5 to $10 (£3.74; £7.47) for eight to 10 hours of recorded work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "We record hands, not faces, and where multi-camera rigs do capture more of the body or environment, we blur faces out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: No names, no contact details, nothing that identifies them personally goes into what we hand off." But his customers are getting more demanding.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Now clients are asking for four to six cameras rigged around a person's head to cover the entire scene, not just the hands.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Getting someone to agree to one small camera is one conversation.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Getting them to agree to wearing what's effectively a five-camera headset is a completely different, and harder, one.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We pay more for that tier of data collection because of what we're asking of people." And the industry is becoming more crowded, Agarwal expects dozens more competitors to emerge in India this year.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Shahil Baig expects dozens more firms to start collecting video of workers Why is such data so important?
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: If you want robots to navigate the real world, they can't just be trained inside computer simulations, argues Manish Agarwal, the founder of Humyn Labs, which collects and processes human-generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Most of that data comes from video, but sometimes collectors wear hardware on their hands and fingers to capture physical contact.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Physical tasks require high-quality signals involving limb movements, fingers, wrists, elbows, shoulders and dynamic force application.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For example: applying the correct grip force so a plastic bottle doesn't crumble versus a steel glass," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: And until recently, that data was not available.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "There is no existing internet archive of embodied human activity - no dataset of a kitchen being cleaned, or a car being assembled by hands that know exactly how much force to apply.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That data has to be captured from scratch, in the real world, across diverse environments," says Agarwal, whose company has bases in Bangalore and San Francisco.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Humyn Labs filters the thousands of hours of video supplied by those collectors, selecting the most useful content.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: It's then labelled so the AI knows what it is looking at and packaged in a format that can be used by clients.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "You need to source across a variety of factories, a variety of tasks, in different geographies because if you want to build deployment for US factories or US houses, you'd want environments that are a proxy for that.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Residential houses in India may not be the right context for building a robotics use case for the US." This video can not be played The factory workers teaching robots how to work like humans But are workers collecting data for machines that will one day do their jobs?
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment it's too early to tell says Bino Paul, senior professor at the School of Management and Labour Studies at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) in Mumbai.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For some workers AI might be a useful tool, but robots could automate other jobs, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The problem is that, if machines do start to take over, there will be little workers can do about.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "By the time workers realise what they have participated in, things may have gone too far," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Like many others, he wants governments to regulate AI.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "AI cannot be viewed merely as a technical system.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We need to develop a socio-technical system in which ethics is upheld through human agency, ensuring that AI delivers beneficence rather than maleficence." Despite concerns over where AI is heading, money is still being poured into its development.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Garments stitching and cutting.

sentences.text: I know this work so well I could probably do it with my eyes closed.

sentences.text: Crime scene evidence is often not enough to identify suspects Randy Gail Sperino was last seen alive on the evening of 9 November 1993, as she was getting into a pickup truck in Granite City, Illinois.

sentences.text: The 34-year-old's body was found hours later in a field nearby, the victim of blunt force trauma.

sentences.text: The identity of her killer was a mystery.

sentences.text: DNA evidence found at the crime scene was tested against standard law enforcement databases, but no matches were found.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: For three decades, investigators from the Madison County Sheriff's Office chased leads and interviewed hundreds of people as they attempted to identify the perpetrator.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The case looked like it would remain one of more than 250,000 unsolved homicides in the US.

sentences.text: Then, last year, detectives tried a fresh approach.

sentences.text: They sent genetic evidence to Othram, a Houston-based company that uses DNA technology to help identify the perpetrators in cold and current crime cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The Madison County detectives had been inspired by investigative genetic genealogy techniques used to identify the Golden State Killer, Joseph James DeAngelo, back in 2018.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: In that case, an investigative team constructed a family tree to help identify the killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They were able to do so thanks to DNA data that relatives had provided to commercial databases, similar to consumer ancestry platforms.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Unlike traditional forensic DNA testing, which generally relies on a direct comparison between evidence and a known person, investigative genetic genealogy can identify distant genetic relatives of an unknown individual.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram set about applying this technique to track down Sperino's killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While the suspect's own DNA profile wasn't available, profiles submitted by his extended relatives allowed the company to identify a male family member.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "That lead broke the case open," said Captain Tim Lawrence of Madison County Sheriff's Office, which was responsible for investigating the crime.

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Yasaman Ghasempour (left) is developing ripeness detection techniques Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector , external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Jing Zhang says new tech has to prove its worth to farmers But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works." Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries , external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The simplest systems need not be expensive.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery , external from $100 (£74) drones.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: On Wednesday, Chancellor John Healy announced the removal of standing charges - fixed daily fees paid regardless of usage - from household gas bills in England, Scotland and Wales, with costs added to the unit rate instead.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: Island Energy said any proposed changes would be subject to consultation with the Communications and and Utilities Regulatory Authority (CURA) on the island.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: A spokesperson warned removing standing charges may benefit some customers but could see others pay more.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: "The cost currently covered by the standing charge would instead be recovered through the unit price of energy," explained an Island Energy spokesperson.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: "This means customers who use less energy could save money, while those who use more could see their bills increase." Islands Energy Group supplies energy to homes and business in Guernsey, Jersey and the Isle of Man.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: The gas utility and energy service provider, which serves about 40,000 domestic, commercial, and industrial customers across the three islands, said any change to the charging structure  would need to have the clear support of the community, the regulator and government.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: CURA have been contacted for a comment.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: Treasury Minister Michael Crowe said his department was reviewing the various measures set out by the chancellor to understand what the implications might be for the island.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: "As we look towards the Isle of Man Budget, in February 2027, our priority is to strike the right balance between supporting people and businesses today and maintaining strong, sustainable public finances for the years ahead," he said.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: In accordance with the Autumn Statement, the island will extend the reduction in the VAT rate, from 5% to 0% on domestic electricity supplies, until 30 June 2027.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: It will also honor the Customs and Excise Agreement with the UK and continue to apply the cut in fuel duty, by 5p per litre, until 30 June 2027.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: A reduced duty rate for red diesel, introduced in June until the end of the year, will also be extended to 30 June 2027.
sentences.article_title: Island Energy: No plans to remove gas standing charge

sentences.text: Businesses in Devon and Cornwall said there were both positives and negatives to the budget Tourism and hospitality leaders have been reacting to this week's Budget.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Among the headlines in chancellor John Healey's first Budget on Wednesday were a £100 payment to help millions of households with energy bills, a VAT cut on electricity bills and a freeze on fuel duty, both extended to July.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: It also announced Devon would get an elected mayor in 2028 white Cornwall was included as the only area on a pathway to become a Foundation Strategic Authority.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Sue Jewell, chair of South East Cornwall Tourism Association and a holiday accommodation provider, said the budget "gave with one hand and took with the other".
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Sue Jewell said the rising minimum wage may lead to some job losses As part of the Budget legal minimum wage is to rise by 3.9% in April Jewell said: "I think it's tricky because actually I would believe that quite a lot of people in our business anyway pay over the minimum wage just to retain staff.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: "However because of the cost we've cut back on staff.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: "Which is sad really because it's local people who could be having local jobs." Dr Harry Pitts, senior lecturer in Politics at the University of Exeter's Cornwall Campus, said the £100 energy payment was one of the "small things to make life a little easier for some households in the immediate period".
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Anyone living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment", funded by extra tax on banks.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Toby Parkins said there was a lot of nervousness ahead of the budget The Budget announced the threshold at which high street shops start paying business rates in England was to be increased from £12,000 to £18,000, meaning businesses would pay no rates on properties with a rateable value below this level.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Toby Parkins, interim ceo at the Cornwall Chamber of Commerce, said he predicted this would benefit about 900 extra businesses in Cornwall.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: "For the small business that is a big win," he said.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Helen Wylde-Archibald, from the Devon Chamber of Commerce, said she "welcomed some stability".
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: "The last two have been a bit scary for business," she said, referring to previous Budgets.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Some farmers said they had not seen much in the Budget that would benefit them James Kittow, from Butcher & Grazier in Cornwall, said: "It just seems like we've been forgotten again.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: "We're an industry that is ready, willing and able to help the country produce the food for the nation." He added there was no change on inheritance tax for farmers.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: Andrea Drew, managing director at Lander Mortgage Services, said the key announcement relating to housing was a scheme for first time buyers, and a a "First Time Buyer Isa".
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: This is an account in which savers can build up a deposit, with the government topping up contributions of up to £4,000 each year with a 25% bonus.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: "The only negative I would say... on new builds, the housing market isn't just all about new builds, it's about existing property... because not everybody wants to have a new build property," she said.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: She added: "The other thing was about the increase in tax for landlords so, they're increasing the tax by 4%." She said she'd seen landlords who decided to sell their property because of the amount of tax but tenants couldn't afford to buy the homes.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements

sentences.text: "What tenants need is more homes to choose from, not fewer, and they can't solve the housing shortage by destroying people who are providing the housing," she said.
sentences.article_title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements
