sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: For students, previously contracts were generally for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Instead, properties are now rented on a rolling basis, which means tenants pay rent weekly or monthly with no fixed end date.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: University-owned halls of residence and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation are exempt , external and can still offer fixed-term contracts so this change primarily affects students renting from a private landlord.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If the Renters' Rights Act wasn't a thing, I don't think I would have been able to move universities because I would have been locked into the full [year] contract," Eddie explains.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Fortunately, Eddie had a friend who was looking for a room who was able to take his place so his housemates could sign a new tenancy.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He acknowledges the situation would have been more difficult for his housemates if there wasn't someone who could take his room.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, Eddie thinks the benefits for students are worth this risk.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If you were to fall out with your flatmates or if you decide that university is not for you, being locked into a full-term contract can be really prohibitive financially," he says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "So without that flexibility, people can really be locked into situations that they don't necessarily want to be in." Lewis Wilson, vice president for higher education at the National Union of Students, says this flexibility means students can also save money on rent by moving home for the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While previously, many student rental contracts ran into the summer after courses had finished, students can now choose to move out earlier if they want.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Wilson says students also benefit from wider changes in the act, which bans landlords in England from evicting tenants without a reason.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Campaigners argue this gives renters greater security and confidence to ask for repairs, without fearing they could be evicted if they raise concerns.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Lewis Wilson from the NUS says the legislation has given students more freedom to move out when they want However, greater flexibility for students to leave tenancies also means less certainty for landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The act did introduce a specific ground , external for landlords to evict a group of students at the end of the academic year if they intend to re-let the property to students.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Chris Norris, chief policy officer at the National Residential Landlords Association, says the bigger problem for student landlords is if their tenants choose to move out earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He argues this is a bigger risk for students - who may fall out with their housemates or drop out of university - than, for example, families, who are less likely to want to move out after just a few months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says the end of fixed-term tenancies means student houses could be left empty over the summer after courses finish - or even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He adds that it is now more difficult for student landlords to rent a house for just a few months as they don't know how long the tenants will stay and can't guarantee it will be available for students again in the autumn.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says it's early days for the new legislation and many landlords are taking this year as a test to see how these issues play out in practice.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, he warns that some may choose to increase the monthly rent they charge to cover the risk of their properties being empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: In some cases, he says landlords may even sell up or stop renting to students, reducing supply and pushing up prices.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue Lawes thinks the changes mean many student landlords will put up their rent Sue Lawes, who rents three shared houses to students in Norwich, is worried about the changes.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While Sue says she doesn't want to put up her prices, if her houses end up being empty over the summer because students decide to end their tenancy after their final exams she says she may have to.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She has already brought forward the start of her tenancy agreements to August instead of September to try and reduce the risks of this.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, she says if her tenants move out earlier in the year she would struggle to make a profit, whilst covering costs including her mortgage, council tax and utility standing charges when the properties are empty.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She argues higher monthly rents would mean bigger upfront costs for students and higher overall costs for those who do choose to carry on renting over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue stresses that she supports the aim of the legislation to give tenants greater security and that students should be able to move out if their landlord is not carrying out repairs.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But she wants landlords to be allowed to offer fixed-term contracts to students in line with the academic year to avoid properties being left empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords are going to find it very, very hard to absorb those void periods," she says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords will put prices up and students are going to pay." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

sentences.text: At Harrow's Bengaluru campus, students wear the traditional Harrow hats and uniforms On the outskirts of Chandigarh city in India's north-western Punjab state, a 473-year-old legacy British public school opened its first all-girls international campus earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: In contrast to the prominent Gothic-style central building on the school grounds in Bedfordshire, England, the Indian premises are more modern, with purpose-built academic blocks.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But a conspicuous red-brick clock tower bears the imprint of the school's British heritage.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: The Bedford School, Mohali, is the newest in at least half a dozen British public schools (elite, fee-paying private schools with a long history), including three of the country's oldest, that have set up shop across the length and breadth of India.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Their expansion comes amid tighter market conditions in China and the introduction of VAT on private school fees in Britain from 1 January 2025.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Since 2023, Bengaluru - India's Silicon Valley and a hub of software and start-up companies - has been home to the prestigious Harrow School, alma mater of India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Queen Elizabeth's School launched in Gurugram near the capital Delhi this August.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Shrewsbury School has a campus in Bhopal in central India, while Wellington College has chosen to set up base in Pune, a western city that calls itself the "Oxford of the East" for its well-regarded universities and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Millfield and a few others are reportedly on their way with satellite campuses in the coming years.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: For decades, India has been home to well-established local boarding schools modelled on the colonial British public-school system, serving elite, aristocratic families.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But this market has rapidly expanded with newly wealthy Indian families increasingly aspiring to give their children more global exposure.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "Our international curriculum is quite a driver for many of them," Caroline Pascoe, head of school at Harrow in Bengaluru, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Harrow and Bedford are among the few schools in India that follow an all-through Cambridge curriculum - a global education framework recognised at 10,000 schools worldwide - from primary through to A-levels.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: He said he was also drawn to the fact the school did not have a "VIP culture" unlike many Indian equivalents.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "All kids are treated the same.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Children of ministers and bureaucrats don't get greater privileges," said Singh.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Beyond the growing ranks of well-heeled local families, non-resident Indians who have either returned home after long stints abroad, or those still in the UK or Middle East wanting their children to connect to their roots, are also a significant market for these schools, says Pascoe.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: There is also a house system - a hallmark of traditional British education.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: These quintessentially parochial quirks are blended with local customs such as singing the Indian national anthem every morning or celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi, a major Hindu festival.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Schools such as Harrow in Bengaluru promote extracurricular activities like music and drama While India's growing economic credentials and burgeoning population of newly minted millionaires are a natural tailwind for expansion, this growth is partly being driven by a slowdown in China.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Much of the expansion of British public schools abroad in the past decade was driven by China and Hong Kong - half of the 151 satellite campuses operated by 50 UK schools are situated in these countries.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But that growth has slowed following changes in regulation, and "increased scrutiny, and even resistance, from national governments", according to a 2025 study by the UK-based Private Education Policy Forum ( PEPF , external ) think tank.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: A new 2024 Chinese law that required schools to integrate patriotic education into all subjects further challenged expansion and even led to planned campuses being cancelled, prompting these schools to consider other locations like India and Vietnam, according to PEPF.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Moreover, in the 2024 Autumn Budget, Britain introduced a 20% VAT on private school fees.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Naomi Atkins, founding principal at Bedford School Mohali, says this has forced many private schools to look overseas.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "They are in a desperate situation.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Even those that hadn't previously looked for international expansion are now suddenly active in India," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Well-heeled local families and non-resident Indians are a major target market for British schools in India But India has not been an easy market, she admits.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Most of these schools are set up in partnership with local investors or operators.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: While in the past schools in other countries might have been able to do deals at 10% of revenue - the fee that they would charge the local partner-investor - margins in India may have shrunk to as low as 1% in some cases, says Atikins.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: There has also been some over-estimation of the size of the market, she says.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Even though India has nearly 250 million children enrolled in schools, English education is deeply entrenched in the country and competition from local players is much more intense compared with other non-English speaking countries like China, Korea or Vietnam.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: India's per capita income is also far lower and the high price-points of the British schools - which can charge up to £15,000 or more for full boarding - can limit growth.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "I've worked in Indonesia, Malaysia and China but Indians are much more price-sensitive - they like a bargain," says Atkins.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: That is why Bedford Mohali has set its fees at roughly half those charged by other British schools.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Between 2011-12 and 2022-23, the satellite campuses of British schools generated £152.4m in profit, according to PEPF, and this profit has grown substantially over the years.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But in India, it appears growth is likely to be slow and steady rather than explosive.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: The country's old colonial roots and new money afford the legacy institutions a significant business opportunity, but it is unlikely to be big enough to offset the loss of the Chinese market, at least immediately.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: A new strategy to restore and enhance protection for nature in Northern Ireland has been launched by the agriculture and environment minister.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: About 40% of the plants and animals in protected sites across Northern Ireland fall short of meeting the standard for "favourable condition".
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: And just one of 49 priority habitat types - like ancient and native woodlands, blanket bogs and species-rich grasslands - have favourable status.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: The Nature Recovery Strategy sets out a long-term framework based on science for tackling biodiversity loss and restoring habitats.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: Andrew Muir says nature must be put "back at the heart of everything we do" Minister Andrew Muir said supporting nature was "not just a nice thing to do" but "a moral obligation to future generations".
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: But the minister acknowledged that money would be needed to address the challenges.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: The strategy highlights the importance of nature as providing the food we eat, the water we drink and the air we breathe.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: Muir said nature must be put "back at the heart of everything we do because when nature thrives, people flourish".
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: "It is essential to a strong economy, healthier communities and a more resilient Northern Ireland," he said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: They can be legally designated to help ensure better management and protection of those species.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: That should lead to work to protect the species and habitats they have been designated for.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: But the Office for Environmental Protection found not enough sites are being designated and the condition of those that have been is worsening .
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: The number of sites that were in favourable condition dropped from 61.7% in 2008, to 51.5% in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: It is now investigating how those sites are being managed , external by the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs, after it found implementation of the designation fell short.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: Northern Ireland is one of the most nature-depleted areas in the world, according to the 2023 State of Nature Report.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: It found 12% of species in Northern Ireland are under threat of extinction, and the number of flowering plants had declined by 14% since 1970.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: The Nature Recovery Strategy identifies six external pressures affecting nature and biodiversity - invasive species; climate change; human impact through inappropriate development; land and sea-use change; increased intensive farming; pollution.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: It says these must all be addressed effectively to allow nature to thrive.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: Ulster Farmers' Union deputy president Glenn Cuddy said his organisation was "still a bit skeptical" about the strategy.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: "There's always a concern that nature will be more thought of than the farming and farmers have been walking along with nature for a long time, even before some of these projects have started," he said.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: "We have always been the guardians of the countryside and for nature too." Heather McLachlan, the National Trust's Northern Ireland director, said: "What really needs to happen is that we need to see where are the priorities.
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: "But of course a strategy isn't everything - we need now to act and take urgent action."
sentences.article_title: Will a new strategy help protect Northern Ireland's nature?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Teens tell BBC of their hopes and fears as they prepare to start work More than four in 10 UK teenagers want more work experience opportunities at school, with a similar proportion calling for more guidance on how to apply for jobs, a survey for the BBC suggests.
sentences.article_title: We asked teens what schools should teach them about work. This is what they said

sentences.text: The online survey, by Survation, , external asked 2,000 young people aged 13 to 18 about the world of work and the help they need to secure employment once they leave full-time education.
sentences.article_title: We asked teens what schools should teach them about work. This is what they said

sentences.text: Some called for more support with their communications skills and raised concerns about stress management and personal finances.
sentences.article_title: We asked teens what schools should teach them about work. This is what they said

sentences.text: Skills Minister Jacqui Smith said it was the government's "mission" to ensure teenagers leave school "confident about their next step and equipped with the skills and experience they need to succeed".
sentences.article_title: We asked teens what schools should teach them about work. This is what they said

sentences.text: When teenagers were asked in the survey what skills or guidance they would like more of at school, the most common responses were more work experience opportunities (44%) and help managing finances (43%).

sentences.text: This video can not be played Meet Jodi: Rare dinosaur skeleton sells for $47.3m The mounted skeleton of a newly-identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex has sold at auction for a colossal $47.3m (£35.5m).
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: Nicknamed Jodi, the roughly 10-foot-tall (3m) skeleton was auctioned by Sotheby's in New York.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The sale comes a year after researchers confirmed that the skeleton belongs to a distinct genus.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The Late Cretaceous carnivore was expected to fetch at least $9m when it went under the hammer on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The auction comes after Sotheby's sold a Tyrannosaurus rex, dubbed Gus, for a record $50.1m in July.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The sale has reignited debate in the scientific community over whether dinosaur remains should be sold privately or displayed publicly.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: Sotheby's described Jodi as an "excellent exhibition-ready" skeleton with about 191 fossil-bone elements and a "beautifully preserved, virtually complete skull".
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The auction house added that the Nanotyrannus is "one of only three such skeletons known to science".
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The specimen is the first to come to market since the existence of the genus was confirmed by US researchers last October, Sotheby's said.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The identify of the buyer, who won after a thrilling 12 minutes of auction bidding between six interested parties, has not been disclosed.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: It becomes the second-most valuable dinosaur fossil ever sold, behind Gus.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The third-most valuable was a Stegosaurus named Apex, which was sold by Sotheby's in July 2024 for $44.6m.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: Megan Jacobs, a palaeontologist at the University of Portsmouth, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Tuesday that Nanotyrannus "was for a very long time believed to be sort of a teenager of T. rex".
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: "But it's a lot smaller and its a lot more gracile.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: So it's very sort-of sleek, slender, [with] blade-like teeth for slicing through meat," Jacobs said.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: Jodi was initially exhibited as a juvenile T. rex at London's Frieze Masters international art fair in October 2023, before the Nanotyrannus genus was classified.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: The skeleton was discovered in the US state of Montana by rancher Jodi Pierson on her land in the Hell Creek Formation, a heavily studied geological site.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: It was later excavated by commercial palaeontologist Clayton Phipps.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: Phipps also discovered the famous "Dueling Dinosaurs" fossil.
sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: That specimen, which shows the remains of a Nanotyrannus and Triceratops apparently in combat, was found eight miles (13km) away from Jodi in 2006.

sentences.text: The "Dueling Dinosaurs" discovery became crucial to the research published by Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli that classified Nanotyrannus as separate from T. rex.

sentences.article_title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction

sentences.text: Waste experts have warned that landfill space in Scotland is rapidly running out Scotland's recycling rate has fallen to its lowest level in five years, according to figures from the Scottish Environment Protection Agency (Sepa).
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: The Scottish government's environmental regulator says households recycled 42.8% of waste in 2025 - down from 44.3% the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: According to a roadmap set by the Scottish government in 2010, recycling rates should have hit 70% last year but are falling well short.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: The share of waste processed at an incinerator remained broadly the same at 82% but the amount being diverted to landfill fell by 10%.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: The Sepa figures show that recycling rates vary massively by local authority.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: South Ayrshire's residents recycled 55% of their waste, compared with 26% in Glasgow.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: The islands have the lowest rates, with Orkney recording a figure of just 18.2%.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: A total of 2.31 million tonnes of waste was created by households in 2025, which represents a fall of just 1,500 tonnes.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: Recycling rates have remained similar - at about 45% - for more than a decade.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: The biggest change has been seen in the way black bag waste is treated.
sentences.article_title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

sentences.text: But this has not happened quickly enough to meet a landfill ban which was due to come in at the start of the year.

sentences.text: It has now been effectively delayed to 2028.

sentences.text: Firefighters said this summer's wildfires were the worst they had experienced Firefighters and the public were knowingly put at risk during this year's wildfires due to chronic underfunding, a union has said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Those working on the ground and in the South Wales control centre said the fires were relentless with injuries "commonplace" for crews.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: The Fire Brigades Union (FBU) said firefighters were climbing hills in unsuitable boots and non-breathable layers used for house fires due to not having enough kit, and there was a "real risk to the public" if immediate action was not taken.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: The Welsh government said it did not provide core funding but "recognise the concerns raised and are clear that we need to do all we can to reduce the risk of wildfires".
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Sean Cayford said some injured firefighters from the wildfires are still not back at work Sean Cayford, a firefighter in Bridgend, said crews were told in mid-August that there were no pumps or fire appliances available across the brigade's entire region.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "I've never heard that before but that was heard again later in the wildfire season.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: That was startling," he said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "We were stretched so thinly," he said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "It has an increasingly destructive effect on the morale of our firefighters.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "It's very difficult to be at a wildfire incident in excess of eight or 10 or 12 hours and not get injured to some degree." He said colleagues had sustained lower limb injuries and heat illness, with many still unable to work.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Gemma Thomas said control room staff were exhausted Gemma Thomas, who works in the control centre, said the average number of calls is usually 200-300 but on their busiest day this summer they had almost 2,000.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "It was just relentless in there," she said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "There were times where we were unable to fulfil the requests that were coming from the incidents.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "We are the first point of contact for somebody who is having potentially the worst day of their life.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "It was so stressful, mentally draining, that you're getting home from work absolutely shattered to think right I've got to go back and do it all again tomorrow." Thomas said there were times when staff needed to take breaks "one at a time for 10 minutes just to get people out of the room".
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "People were getting to the point where they were just shattered in work, shattered at home," she said, adding there was no work-life balance because they needed to use free time to rest.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Thomas said support from management was "phenomenal" and "even the firefighters on the ground were understanding how stretched we were in the control room".
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: But she does not believe they could sustain it long-term and wants to see an increase in numbers of firefighters.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: A wildfire above Cwm, Ebbw Vale, in August First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth held a climate change and resilience summit in Merthyr Tydfil on Thursday, which brought "key partners together to develop future actions".
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: It hosted representatives from the fire services, police, local government, farmers and climate change organisations.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "There was poor preparation," said Gareth Tovey, executive council member for Wales, explaining they redirected specialist crews such as water teams to the wildfires.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "At some stages there was zero crew back up for vast parts of south Wales," he said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "Firefighters were injured because they didn't have the right kit to fight wildfires." The FBU said there was a shortfall of 400 firefighters in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Tovey said the union had been warning "for years" authorities needed to do something and there was a "real risk to the public" if immediate action was not taken.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: He said bringing in the Army , was "not a silver bullet" as they do not have the firefighting skills needed.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: An FBU survey following the fires found 69% of firefighters felt significantly under-equipped, with just 8% feeling fully equipped.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Nearly half reported welfare facilities during wildfire deployment were insufficient.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Firefighters are funded by the public but through a levy decided by the local authority for the area.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: This is part of their budget, which is in turn set by the Welsh government.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: North Wales Fire and Rescue Service was applying to the Welsh government's emergency assistance scheme to cover the additional cost of the wildfires this summer.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: While the full financial impact is still being assessed, the cost was expected to exceed £500,000.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: At one point firefighters in north Wales were managing six wildfires at once - more than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: It comes as a report from the UK's Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee said the wildfires left firefighters working in extreme conditions and exposed weaknesses in the UK's resilience and preparation.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: It called for a UK government-funded "national wildfire prevention campaign" with clear and consistent messaging, along with wildfire risk indicators in weather forecasts.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "This is a government now that is building that network of partners that showed real determination at the summit this morning to deal with what is clearly now a very very real challenge in the here and now." He declined to confirm there would be more funding.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "There is no escaping from the fact that we face very real financial challenges," he said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: The Welsh government said individual fire and rescue authorities determine how many firefighters they need and set their budgets accordingly.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "They should take this summer's wildfires into account when doing so," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service's chief fire officer Craig Flannery added climate-related emergencies were having a real impact on communities, environment and public services, and require a collective effort.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Natural Resources Wales' (NRW) national operations executive director, Dominic Driver, said: "The impacts of this summer's significant wildfires are still being felt across the country, going far beyond the visible scars left on the landscape.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "They can be seen in the habitats destroyed, carbon stores depleted and damaged soils that will take many years to regenerate and recover.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: "We are focused on supporting nature's recovery and building resilience to this increasing challenge posed by climate change." He said NRW would be prioritising work to make Wales more climate-resilient.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: When we landed by helicopter at Rosebank, this oil field was at the centre of a political storm - and set to be in the path of a real one.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: We arrived on Wednesday morning, just a few hours after the UK government had granted consent for the production of gas from the Jackdaw field in the North Sea.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: But already attention was shifting to this wild and windy patch of the North Atlantic – the next big decision for Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Rosebank is bigger than Jackdaw, it would generate higher greenhouse gas emissions, and it could be far more lucrative for its owners, Adura and Ithaca.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Nicola Boyd loves her job on the Petrojarl Rosebank vessel This summer, along with a camera crew, I travelled to Jackdaw, 150 miles east of Aberdeen.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Now we were the first journalists to visit Rosebank.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: We came here - days before Storm Boelo arrived with strong winds and heavy rain - to scrutinise a controversial project which is at the heart of a national debate about climate change, energy policy and the economy.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: But we also hoped for a rare glimpse into life offshore.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "It's good fun, it's interesting, every day can change," said Nicola Boyd, who runs the helideck, and greeted us as we struggled out of our lifejackets and survival suits.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Boyd has worked offshore for nearly a decade, including a year on Rosebank - where she spends two weeks at a time followed by three weeks' leave.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "It's a job I love," she added.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: The Petrojarl Rosebank is moored in the North Atlantic waiting to see if production gets the go-ahead from the UK government It's also a job that calls for steady legs and a strong stomach.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Unlike the fixed Jackdaw platform, this installation – 80 miles north west of Shetland – is a large ship, a floating production, storage and offloading vessel (FPSO) named the Petrojarl Rosebank.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: It's been chartered by the field's owners from Aberdeen-based Altera and, during my 48 hours on board, it was constantly but gently rolling on the North Atlantic swell.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Those conditions may be misleading.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Ewan Leonard says the winter weather can be "a bit of a challenge" The deep reserves of skill, ingenuity and engineering prowess among the 122 people on board are obvious.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: The jobs are well-paid and, according to Ewan Leonard, the facilities are excellent.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "We have single-man cabins, there's good gym facilities, there's a lot of rec rooms here." Douglas Hogge, a production supervisor in charge of a team responsible for the safe extraction of oil and gas, agrees.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "There's the gym, the sauna," he said, adding "you can obviously go and get some fresh air.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: There's plenty of fresh air out there." Food on board the ship was described as "fantastic" "As you've seen yourself, the food is fantastic on board, so no complaints." added Leonard.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Everyone we spoke to agreed with that, praising the talented chefs who sent out all sorts of delicious dishes, from braised ox cheek to mackerel to pork loin, day and night.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: As dusk gathers and the nightshift get ready for work with a strange breakfast of fillet steak and chocolate brownie pudding, the vessel begins to glow in the gloom.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: It is a strange sight, the decks criss-crossed by a bewilderingly complex array of pipes, valves and bright yellow steelwork.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: The ship is an array of pipes, valves and bright yellow steelwork The ship doesn't move far, rotating around a fixed central point called the turret to face into the weather, making life a little easier for those on board.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: If production is approved, oil and gas will be pumped up through the turret from wells in the field below, which contains an estimated 300m to 500m barrels, enough for perhaps 25 years.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "For myself and a lot of the guys, that would see us out to retirement," said Douglas Hogge.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "We need to see this approved," he added.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Environmental campaigners strongly disagree.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: They've been trying to stop Rosebank for years, with some success.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "The future of the energy sector in the UK is renewable energy," said Tessa Khan, executive director of the campaigning group Uplift.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Consent for production at Rosebank was first granted under the Conservative government in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: But in 2025, after a challenge by Greenpeace and Uplift, the Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled the approvals of the UK's largest known untapped oil field and Jackdaw were unlawful because they had failed to take into account the climate impact of actually burning the fossil fuels in cars, homes and factories.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: The judge, Lord Ericht, said the fields' developers could carry on with work short of producing oil and gas while they provided more detailed environmental assessments for the government and regulators to consider.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "We think Rosebank would be a disastrous decision and a terrible deal for ordinary people across this country," said Khan, urging prime minister Andy Burnham to prioritise renewables in his quest to re-industrialise the nation.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "If the government's interested in building investor confidence, giving the green light to a major new oil field is going to do the opposite," she argued.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Whatever happens with Rosebank and Jackdaw, the long-term trend for the industry is clear and it is one of decline.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: It's a quarter of a century since oil production peaked and in recent years jobs in oil and gas have been disappearing much faster than they're being created in renewable energy such as wind and solar power.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: The oil from Rosebank would be loaded onto tankers via a gigantic hose and nozzle, which looks like the super-sized pump of an enormous floating filling station.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: From there it would be sold on the international market and, most likely, taken to continental Europe for refining.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Opponents say that proves the project is of little benefit to the UK and should be rejected.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Supporters argue that's not the case because UK and European energy markets are co-dependent, adding that Rosebank will generate millions in tax for the Treasury.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Neil McCulloch, chief executive of Adura – which owns 80% of Rosebank and is a joint venture between Shell and the Norwegian state energy firm, Equinor – is optimistic.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: He points out that Rosebank contains not just oil but gas which would be piped to Shetland and on to the St Fergus terminal in Aberdeenshire, with the potential to heat 500,000 British homes at peak production.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: Approval of this project, argues McCulloch, could pave the way for four more Jackdaw-sized gas developments in the waters west of Shetland – Tornado, Tornado East, Tobermory and Suilven.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "We would like to proceed with them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: A surge in fossil fuel production if Rosebank is approved is exactly what campaigners fear.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: It would, argues Tessa Khan, exacerbate the deadly and damaging impact of climate change for British teachers, nurses, firefighters and families worried about their children while making "huge profits for companies that are already incredibly profitable".
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: The oil from Rosebank would be loaded onto tankers via a gigantic hose and nozzle When it comes to the impending UK government decision – which sources have told BBC News should come before Christmas – there is a strange mood at Rosebank.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: The decision in favour of Jackdaw has clearly encouraged many on board but it has also highlighted the jeopardy they are facing.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: For now, most workers we spoke to said they were just focusing on the job, with its strange rhythms and unusual restrictions – no ability to pop to the shops, no alcohol, a lot of special occasions missed.

sentences.text: And for some on board, very particular cravings.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: For steward Liam Davidson, it is a desire to see his French bulldog, Bailey, at the end of his fortnight on board.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "My wee dog's at the heliport when I arrive," he said, "I do miss her." It is hoped the decision on Rosebank will be made in the next few weeks For Nicola Boyd, it's her double bed and a pizza delivery.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: "I love seeing the family, but for me, it's the pizza," she told me.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: But this time there might be a delay in delivering Boyd herself.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: She is coming to the end of her fortnight but, as she helped us into our survival suits, the Met Office issued an amber weather warning for much of Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm

sentences.text: For Rosebank, it seems, there are stormy seas ahead, one way or another.

sentences.text: Microsoft boss Satya Nadella Technology giant Microsoft says its profits for the three months to the end of September jumped to more than $36.6bn (£27.5bn), just days after announcing plans to cut its workforce by more than a quarter.

sentences.text: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing Until a few years ago many of us may have been blissfully unaware of what a data centre was.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: These giant, warehouse-like buildings power virtually all our internet activity, from our web searches and emails to movie downloads and online banking.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: They are at the heart of the AI boom, housing the advanced computer chips and servers needed to run services like ChatGPT and Claude.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But the speed at which they're growing, the enormous amount of electricity they consume and concerns about their environmental impact are fuelling a public backlash around the world.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: In the US, they've become a huge issue ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, with both Republicans and opposition Democrats coming out against their development.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: It's putting opponents of data centre expansion on a collision course with US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed the pushback as a "sick conspiracy", even as public anger grows.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the data centre boom, and why opposition is growing.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: There are about 12,250 data centres around the world, according to Data Center Map , external , a company that tracks both operational and pre-operational sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: That's up sharply from 2021, when there were around 8,000 , external operational sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: As the chart below shows, data centres are most densely clustered in the US which has 4,767 sites.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: It is followed by Europe, where the UK and Germany lead.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Data centres have typically been located near to cities where it's easier to access high voltage power lines or water resources for cooling.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But as they get bigger, more are being built in rural areas.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But when it comes to actual capacity, the US is ahead by a much larger margin, with China in second place and Europe lagging far behind.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: This gap is set to widen in the coming years, leading some to warn Europe risks missing out on the potential economic benefits of the AI boom , external .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Data centres vary wildly in size, ranging from ones that fit inside a garden shed to others covering vast expanses of land.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: The world's largest operational data centre is widely reported to be one run by China Telecom in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, covering an area of approximately one million square metres (10.7 million sq ft).
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: That is equivalent to about 140 Fifa football pitches.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: However, much larger sites are under construction as the graphic below shows.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: All these sites are being built exclusively to provide the immense computing power needed to run AI services.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: For instance, Colossus 2, which is part of the wider Colossus campus, will house hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips made by tech giant Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: It will also be used to train xAI's chatbot Grok.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Elon Musk's company will use 41 methane gas turbines to help power the site, which activists say could "significantly increase" local air pollution , external .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Local regulators say the turbines will meet air quality standards.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: The pressure data centres put on local resources has sparked increasing concern.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: These facilities can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, which could lead to water shortages , some experts say.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Data centres worldwide are also thought to consume more electricity than the whole of France, as the chart below shows.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: This growing hunger for power is driving up carbon emissions, analysis shows , while putting pressure on local grids, which some fear could push up energy prices .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: With others worried about the noise data centres make and the space they take up, a public backlash is gathering steam.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Some 16 US states have proposed laws to ban or temporarily block new facilities, and it could be a key issue in November's midterm elections .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Outside the US, opposition to data centres has emerged in countries like Mexico , France, Indonesia and the UK .
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But supporters say data centres are critical to national security , and the development of AI.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: They also say they are good for the economy , external , attracting investment, generating tax revenue and creating jobs in areas like construction.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: A recent report by the Brookings Center , external suggests data centres do create local jobs, although fewer than industry advocates claim.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: The type of data centre matters too.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: So-called hyperscale facilities - massive sites owned and run by tech giants like Amazon and Microsoft - have a bigger positive effect on jobs, it found.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But "colocation" facilities, which lease space to remote tenants without a local presence, brought fewer benefits.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: As the debate over their merits intensifies, the data centre rollout continues.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: This year, the tech industry is expected to spend a combined $765bn , external ($544bn) on AI infrastructure in 2026, with this topping $1tn next year.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: But as concerns about the environmental impact grow, the tech industry is exploring alternatives.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: One idea is to put data centres in space , external or on the Moon , where they could harness abundant solar energy.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Others predict that more AI processing could eventually be carried out by the hardware already inside our computers and smartphones , reducing the need for vast data centres altogether.
sentences.article_title: Big, noisy and coming to a town near you - why the data centre backlash is growing

sentences.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) firm Anthropic just released the required paperwork ahead of its long-anticipated debut on the US stock market.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The 335-page document included fresh details of how the Claude chatbot owner makes money, what it spends that money on and who it is controlled by.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic also detailed some of the risks it claimed AI technology poses, including how it could take human lives.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: That information sat alongside the many purported benefits of the technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Here are five key points worth highlighting from the filing.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Every public company has to tell potential investors how things could go wrong.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic's "risk factors" were unique, also disclosing how the AI technology it is developing could doom humanity as a whole.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "Sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," Anthropic said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: It noted that less than a year ago, a hacking group Anthropic believed to be sponsored by China "manipulated" Claude to successfully intrude on a number of institutions, including large technology companies, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing companies and government agencies.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: But Anthropic said its success is dependent on its ability to constantly "develop, improve, and deploy the most advanced, capable, and useful AI models".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: One of the most significant risks to that ability is Anthropic's access to infrastructure it needs, including computer chips and data centres, to build, train and operate the models that underpin its technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic has yet to disclose a target share price for its stock listing.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The company is widely expected to debut with a market valuation of $2 trillion or more, making it the largest stock listing in history.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: But the figure will be heavily influenced by its financial performance.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The company's overall revenue was $16.2bn for the six-month period.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Revenues are rising rapidly, but the firm has a long way to go before it breaks even.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Hooper said such large costs are expected to grow.

sentences.text: Even with this kind of cash, it won't be enough to maintain its business growth.

sentences.text: "I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI.

sentences.text: Actor Robert Rhodes says people with visible differences experience the same key emotions as those without An actor is backing a charity's call for more positive roles for performers with scars and visible differences.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: One casting agency said visible differences were often used as a shorthand for villainy, but that these casting briefs could be successfully challenged.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: New research by the Centre for Appearance Research (CAR) at the University of the West of England showed that people who are exposed to visible difference via villainous characters go on to have a more negative perception of people with visible difference in the real world, the charity said.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: Rhodes, who was recently in the BBC One show, The Rapture, was born with a large facial birthmark as a result of congenital melanocytic nevus and was left with scarring following multiple surgeries to remove it as a child.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: He said: "We can't wait for action any longer.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: "Yes, there is often trauma associated with a scar, but we experience joy, love and success just like everyone else.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: "I want children growing up with visible differences to see characters who look like them being heroes, friends, parents and love interests – not just villains." About 4.9 million people in the UK have a visible difference, the charity said.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: As part of its work to monitor visible difference representation, it has worked with the Creative Diversity Network to include visible difference as a category in its diversity data monitoring and reporting.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: Louise Wright, chief executive of Changing Faces, said: "For years we've asked the industry to think about the stories it tells about visible difference.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: "Now, for the first time, we have proof that those stories don't stay on screen – they shape how people with visible difference are treated in real life.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: "Halloween is the moment this is impossible to ignore, which is why we're asking industry, and the public, to help us change it." Bailey Frances, from Cambridge-based Shakyra Dowling Casting, a member of the Casting Directors' Association, said: "Getting it right matters.
sentences.article_title: Actor targets 'scarred villain' screen stereotype

sentences.text: "Villains are often written with visible differences (eg facial scars) as shorthand, but asking whether a character could be interpreted differently, or whether that difference is essential to the story, leads to better, more truthful storytelling," she said.

sentences.text: An artist's impression of how the Littlewoods building could look after its redevelopment into a film and television production campus The government has pledged £20m towards plans to transform Liverpool's derelict Littlewoods building into a film and television production campus.

sentences.text: It is unclear whether the money will be enough to meet the project's funding needs - Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram previously sought £50m in government support .
sentences.article_title: Liverpool's Littlewoods film studios plan given £20m Budget boost

sentences.article_title: Liverpool's Littlewoods film studios plan given £20m Budget boost

sentences.article_title: Liverpool's Littlewoods film studios plan given £20m Budget boost

sentences.article_title: Liverpool's Littlewoods film studios plan given £20m Budget boost

sentences.article_title: Liverpool's Littlewoods film studios plan given £20m Budget boost

sentences.article_title: Liverpool's Littlewoods film studios plan given £20m Budget boost

sentences.article_title: Liverpool's Littlewoods film studios plan given £20m Budget boost

sentences.text: The Bamboo Club opened in 1966 as a social hub for Bristol's Caribbean community The young promoters' experiences echo a much longer history of black Bristolians having to create their own spaces for music and social life.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Many black people were turned away from existing clubs and bars in Bristol during the 1960s, which led to the creation of  "blues parties", un-licensed house parties where people danced to genres such as ska, reggae and rocksteady.
